chunks: Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the child of al-mula'ana (conjugal imprecation), who inherits him? He said, 'His mother.' I said, 'If his mother dies, who inherits him?' He said, 'His maternal uncles.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits the child of al-mula'ana if the mother dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific inheritance lineage for the child of *al-mula'ana*, a case where a husband and wife invoke curses upon each other to prove innocence of adultery. It establishes that the mother is the primary heir, and upon her death, the inheritance passes to the maternal uncles (*akhwal*), reflecting the Shia juristic view that the paternal line is severed due to the imprecation. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia interpretation of how the paternal bond is nullified in this specific legal scenario.
